why.why: major: Location filter silently drops MsgPack003 about an in-compilation type reached through a metadata generic

not_met: claude: The existing suite passes (170/170, no new failures), so the parenthetical part holds, but the clause's main statement does not: the location filter also drops diagnostics about types declared in the current compilation when the reporting location is a metadata member. My probe (scratch worktree, SDK 8, not in facts.json): metadata generic class Lib.Item<T> with [Key(0)] T Content, used as Item<Foo> where App.Foo lacks [MessagePackObject]; base reports MsgPack003 'Type must be marked with MessagePackObjectAttribute: Item.Content', head reports nothing. Item<T> as a class did not crash on base (issue table: 'class Item<T> | ok'), so this is a regression in a configuration that worked before. The existing suite does not cover it.; reviewers_disagree: claude says not_met, codex says met, nemotron says met

I saw the generator emit Formatters.App.R.Lib.ItemFormatter`1.g.cs in my probe but did not execute it.)

requirements.text: Building a project whose [MessagePackObject] type has a member of a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly must not crash the source generator (no CS8785) and must produce a generated resolver.

claude.basis: Root cause confirmed: Roslyn imports private fields of metadata structs, so the compiler-generated backing field of Item<T> looks like an unkeyed member and the base field path indexed DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] unconditionally (outside the ?.Invoke), crashing the generator as well as the analyzer; head uses FirstOrDefault there, the three new tests (which also run the generator and assert the resolver hint name and no warnings) pass at head and all 3 fail on base source; my own probe of the exact issue repro (record struct Item<T> in a metadata reference) gave CS8785 + no files on base and App.R.g.cs with no generator diagnostics on head. Runtime round-trip of the generated resolver was not executed (tests.execution not run for this change), so only 'produces a resolver' is established, not that it serializes Item<int> correctly.

requirements.text: Diagnostics about members of a type declared in a referenced assembly must not be reported at locations outside the compilation being analyzed.

claude.basis: Every analyzer diagnostic now passes through ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, which only forwards diagnostics whose location is in a syntax tree of the current compilation. I checked that this filter is what makes ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember pass: with only the filter reverted (FirstOrDefault kept) that test fails with two location-less MsgPack004 diagnostics for MyGenericStruct.Unkeyed (my own run, not in facts.json). So the clause is enforced. It is over-enforced, though: see finding C1.

codex.basis: The change filters analyzer diagnostics to source locations belonging to this compilation and uses nullable syntax-reference lookups for members that may come from metadata.

findings.title: Location filter silently drops MsgPack003 about an in-compilation type reached through a metadata generic
findings.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every diagnostic whose location is not a source location in this compilation, including Location.None and metadata locations, which Roslyn does allow analyzers to report. TypeMustBeMessagePackObject (MsgPack003) is located at callerSymbol.Locations[0]; when the caller is a member of a referenced generic (Lib.Item<T>.Content) and T is an app type without [MessagePackObject] (Item<Foo>), the diagnostic is about App.Foo but is now discarded. My probe: base reports MsgPack003 (metadata location), head reports nothing, while the generator still emits App.R.g.cs and a formatter for Lib.Item`1, so the missing Foo formatter would only surface at run time. This configuration (a generic class from another assembly) did not crash on base, so it is a regression. The XML doc comment's justification ('which analyzers are not permitted to do') is only true for source locations in other compilations.

evidence.quote: which analyzers are not permitted to do

evidence.note: facts.json: tests.full_suite pass: tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests: 170 tests, 170 passed, 0 failed (0 not failing on base, 0 also failing on base)

findings.suggested_fix: Instead of dropping, relocate: when a diagnostic's location is not in this compilation, re-report it at the nearest in-compilation location (the member of the type being analyzed that led to the metadata type, i.e. the outermost callerSymbol), or keep dropping only diagnostics about the metadata type's own members (MsgPack004/005) and let MsgPack003 for in-compilation types through. Add a test with a metadata generic class and an unattributed app type argument.

findings.title: BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull is now silently suppressed for positional record properties in source
findings.claim: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null when the property's syntax is a ParameterSyntax (positional record), so with the filter the diagnostic becomes Location.None and is dropped. My probe on '[MessagePackObject] public record Cmd([property: Key(null)] string Scope)': base threw AD0001 InvalidCastException (the old hard cast), head reports no key diagnostic at all. Better than a crash, but an in-source invalid contract is no longer reported; no test covers line 985.
findings.suggested_fix: Fall back to ParameterSyntax.Identifier (as the MemberNeedsKey path at line 926 already does) and add a test for a positional record with Key(null).

findings.title: Fix treats the symptom location; metadata struct backing fields are still walked as members
findings.claim: The crash comes from Roslyn importing private (compiler-generated backing) fields of metadata structs, which GetObjectInfo then treats as unkeyed members. The change makes those diagnostics location-safe and filters them, but still builds diagnostics for compiler-generated fields; any future diagnostic path that dereferences syntax for fields of a metadata struct will crash the same way. Skipping members without source/with CompilerGeneratedAttribute for metadata types would remove the class of bug.

trust.text: Building a project whose [MessagePackObject] type has a member of a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly must not crash the source generator (no CS8785) and must produce a generated resolver.
trust.label: proven
trust.why: All 3 reviewers say met (16 verified citations); build, tests.targeted pass

checks.summary: 19 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (3 new tests in run)

reviewers.basis: Root cause confirmed: Roslyn imports private fields of metadata structs, so the compiler-generated backing field of Item<T> looks like an unkeyed member and the base field path indexed DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] unconditionally (outside the ?.Invoke), crashing the generator as well as the analyzer; head uses FirstOrDefault there, the three new tests (which also run the generator and assert the resolver hint name and no warnings) pass at head and all 3 fail on base source; my own probe of the exact issue repro (record struct Item<T> in a metadata reference) gave CS8785 + no files on base and App.R.g.cs with no generator diagnostics on head. Runtime round-trip of the generated resolver was not executed (tests.execution not run for this change), so only 'produces a resolver' is established, not that it serializes Item<int> correctly.

The new metadata-reference tests pass with the change and fail when the source is reverted; the added collector logic handles missing source declarations and drops diagnostics outside the analyzed compilation.

Three new metadata-reference tests pass on head with zero analyzer/generator diagnostics and the expected resolver hint name is generated, while on base the same input threw IndexOutOfRangeException in the shared TypeCollector path (surfaced as AD0001), and the head generator run explicitly asserts no diagnostics at Warning or above.

trust.text: Diagnostics about members of a type declared in a referenced assembly must not be reported at locations outside the compilation being analyzed.
trust.label: proven
trust.why: All 3 reviewers say met (11 verified citations); build, tests.targeted pass

checks.summary: 19 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (3 new tests in run)

reviewers.basis: Every analyzer diagnostic now passes through ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, which only forwards diagnostics whose location is in a syntax tree of the current compilation. I checked that this filter is what makes ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember pass: with only the filter reverted (FirstOrDefault kept) that test fails with two location-less MsgPack004 diagnostics for MyGenericStruct.Unkeyed (my own run, not in facts.json). So the clause is enforced. It is over-enforced, though: see finding C1.
The change filters analyzer diagnostics to source locations belonging to this compilation and uses nullable syntax-reference lookups for members that may come from metadata.

ReportIfLocatedInCompilation only forwards a diagnostic when its location is in source and its syntax tree is contained in the compilation being analyzed; GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null for metadata-declared properties, producing Location.None diagnostics that are dropped, so no member diagnostic from a referenced assembly is reported at an outside location.
